trust_decision.summary: Keys that collide with Object.prototype members (toString, valueOf, hasOwnProperty, constructor) arriving from untrusted input must be resolved as own properties, decided by Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty guards at flatten's nested-record write and at the intersect merge; the truthiness test and the `in` operator both resolve them to inherited members.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names flatten() and record() issue paths, so the first look is the `if (flatErrors.nested![dotPath])` test: for dotPath 'toString' it reads Object.prototype.toString (a function, truthy) and the next line calls .push on it, throwing TypeError.

fix_sites.entry_point: flatten() public error-formatting method (v.flatten), fed issue paths produced by record()/object() ~run
intersect() and intersectAsync() schemas, via _merge at intersect.ts:151 and intersectAsync.ts:161
fix_sites.module_kind: internal schema utility (@internal merge helper) under schemas/intersect/utils

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory only says flatten() throws on record() paths, and _merge is an @internal helper of the intersect schema that the report never names; a solver can argue the merge hunk is a different feature whose worst effect is a spurious validation issue, not a crash, so it is out of the reported scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: flatten() must keep appending to the existing message array when several issues share one dot path (the published test pins a plain-prototype result with toStrictEqual, so Object.create(null) or a Map breaks it), and _merge() must keep merging equal objects, arrays and Dates and return {issue:true} only on a real conflict; an over-broad fix that reuses _isValidObjectKey (which rejects 'constructor') also stops accumulating messages for that key.

O6_input_shapes: issue path whose only key is an Object.prototype member: 'toString', 'valueOf', 'hasOwnProperty', 'constructor'
repeated issues for the same colliding key: the message array must accumulate rather than be replaced
colliding key only at the top level; a nested path such as 'a.toString' can never collide because getDotPath joins keys with '.'
non-colliding dot paths ('user.name', array index '0') must be byte-identical in the result
object merge where the colliding key is own on the second value only, on both with equal values, and on both with conflicting values
non-plain values (Date, array, primitives) that must still merge or fail exactly as before

O7_producer.where: library/src/schemas/record/record.ts:145-151 builds the ObjectPathItem with key = the untrusted input key; library/src/utils/getDotPath/getDotPath.ts:32-48 turns it into the string flatten keys on

O8_uncovered_routes.route: An object carrying an own 'constructor' key never enters the deep-merge branch because the plain-object guard tests value1.constructor === Object (line 34), so intersect([object({}), object({constructor: string()})]) still reports a spurious type issue after the published fix
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The guard is how valibot detects a plain object versus a Date, array or class instance, and the advisory and its tests never mention 'constructor' in a merge, so a solver can call it intended behaviour.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the second fix site, one line above the changed hunk

O8_uncovered_routes.route: object()/objectAsync() presence check `key in input`: a schema entry named 'toString' is treated as present in input even when input has no such own key, so the inherited function is validated and an issue path with key 'toString' is produced
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The entry name comes from the developer's schema definition, not from untrusted record input, and the advisory only mentions record() issue paths; the effect is a wrong issue, not the TypeError.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: library/src/schemas/object (a different top-level area from methods/flatten), reached only through a second schema

O8_uncovered_routes.route: strictObject() unknown-key loop `!(key in this.entries)`: an own input key named 'toString' is treated as a declared entry, so it is neither reported as an unknown key nor copied to the output
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Entries are developer-defined plain objects and the affected key is an odd schema name; the advisory is about error formatting, and strictObject's own contract already says extra keys are rejected by design.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: looseObject()/objectWithRest() rest copy `_isValidObjectKey(input, key) && !(key in this.entries)`: an own input key named 'toString' passes the own-key test but is dropped instead of being copied or validated by rest
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The rest feature is about unknown keys and the guard was written for prototype-pollution safety, so a solver can read the inherited hit as a deliberate security exclusion.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: library/src/schemas/looseObject and library/src/schemas/objectWithRest, two more schema packages

O8_uncovered_routes.route: flatten() still mishandles the key '__proto__': the hasOwnProperty test is false, so the else branch assigns flatErrors.nested['__proto__'] = [message], which sets the prototype instead of creating a key, and the message is silently lost
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: record() already excludes '__proto__' at record.ts:135, so only a computed-key object schema entry can produce that path, and it does not throw.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same hunk as the published flatten fix
